result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in File & Path Security: 3 FOUND, 2 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Full-repository application source/configuration review, not a diff review. Traced multipart metadata through UploadAsync and blob publication. Verified Azure.Storage.Blobs 12.9.1 upstream implementation: https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/Azure.Storage.Blobs_12.9.1/sdk/storage/Azure.Storage.Blobs/src/BlobClient.cs#L1565-L1575 opens new FileStream(path, FileMode.Open, FileAccess.Read). Static exploit paths only; no live requests executed. NOT_FOUND means no confirmed pattern, not proof of absence. UploadAsync(string) reads a server-local file rather than the multipart InputStream; therefore arbitrary client-content upload was not assumed.

values.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
values.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync passes attacker-controlled multipart files[i].FileName directly to BlobClient.UploadAsync(string path), which opens that path on the server instead of reading the uploaded InputStream. After Index initializes the shared container, a crafted multipart filename naming a process-readable server file causes that file's contents to be copied into blob storage. Index lists blob URIs and creates new containers with PublicAccessType.Blob, exposing copied data when public access is permitted. No authentication or path confinement is present. Requires a configured writable storage account and a readable existing target. This and CWE-23/CWE-36 are three classifications of one root cause, not three independent defects.

values.name: Relative Path Traversal
values.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync sends the unmodified multipart filename to the server-local path overload of BlobClient.UploadAsync. A crafted filename such as ../target.txt or ..\target.txt traverses relative to the server process working directory when the target exists and the process can read it. GetRandomBlobName only transforms the destination blob name; it does not sanitize the local source path. The resulting blob is discoverable through Index. Same root cause as CWE-22; exploitation depends on working-directory layout, storage configuration, and file permissions.

values.name: Absolute Path Traversal
values.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: A manually crafted multipart filename such as C:\Windows\win.ini reaches BlobClient.UploadAsync(string path) unchanged in HomeController.UploadAsync. On the intended Windows host this selects an absolute server-local file rather than uploaded content, and copies a process-readable target to the configured blob container. There is no root/path allowlist. Same root cause as CWE-22; requires a successful Index initialization, storage access, and target read permission.

values.name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
values.description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.

values.name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
values.description: The product processes an XML document that can contain XML entities with URIs that resolve to documents outside of the intended sphere of control, causing the product to embed incorrect documents into its output.
